arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01 originating from a phishing email that delivered a malicious PowerShell payload. The payload executed via Outlook, launched a hidden PowerShell process, and loaded an unsigned DLL through rundll32.exe from the user's Temp directory. This established command-and-control (C2) communication over TCP/443 to 198.51.100.23. Initial reconnaissance was conducted from external IP 185.220.101.42, which previously performed an Nmap SYN scan against an internal IT host (WS-IT-101). Despite detection by EDR and NDR systems, containment actions (firewall block, EPP quarantine, IAM lockout) were denied due to policy or evidence gaps. No sandbox detonation confirmed malicious behavior, highlighting a detection gap for fileless and living-off-the-land techniques.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 performs Nmap SYN scan against WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged as low-severity scan event.
User CORP\jsmith launches Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.

PowerShell downloads and executes unsigned beacon.dll via rundll32.exe from Temp directory.
Beacon establishes persistent C2 channel to 198.51.100.23:443.
Host file modification detected on WS-FIN-AP01, likely to block security domains.
EDR alerts on suspicious process chain and C2 traffic. Incident response initiated.
Containment actions (firewall block, EPP quarantine, user lockout) denied due to lack of approval or insufficient evidence linkage.
